title.narrative: Improving Access to Essential WASH Assistance for Vulnerable Rural and Under-served Households in Beletweyne District.

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian situation in Somalia continues to be high with a rapidly deteriorating humanitarian situation experienced since the last quarter of 2024 and continuing into 2025. This is driven by compounding climatic shocks, conflict, displacement and inadequate humanitarian funding. Persistent La Nina conditions, below-average and delayed Gu rains along with localized flooding have disrupted seasonal patterns and significantly strained WASH infrastructure.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtA January 2025 report by OCHA Somalia, identified that poor access to clean WASH as a major contributor to deteriorating health outcomes in affected communities. Additionally, inadequate WASH services was reported as an important factor in driving the spread of acute diarrheal diseases and contributing to high levels of acute malnutrition among children.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt Beledweyne district remains one of the hardest-hit areas in Somalia by recurring floods. The floods in May and November 2024 caused widespread damage including destroying shelters, submerging or contaminating water sources and leading to latrines either overflowing or being washed away. These triggered significant displacement of both IDPs and host community memberslt/pgtltpgtltbrgt An assessment by the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) in March 2025 revealed that reduction in WASH interventions brought about by inadequate funding is expected to escalate the persistent risk of water borne diseases and forcing communities in Beledweyne to rely on unsafe water sources. Additionally, the assessment found that the November 2024 flood in Beledweyne had damaged or destroyed WASH infrastructure, such as water supply systems, sanitation facilities and hygiene promotion materials making it difficult for people to access clean water and sanitation serviceslt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe protection risks for women, girls and persons with disabilities due to inadequate WASH services are significant. A UNFPA report from August 2024 highlighted their increased vulnerability to GBV when fetching water or using latrines, especially at night. Pregnant and lactating women and Persons with disabilities face even greater riskslt/pgtltpgtltbrgtHIWA's proposed project aims to improve critical WASH needs in 5 targeted villages and 8 IDP camps in Beledweyne district. In the water component, HIWA plans to construct and equip 17 shallow wells with hand pumps, ensuring a sustainable access to water supply as well as construct 2 elevated water tank.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the sanitation component, HIWA proposes to construct 24 latrines designed to be easily accessible for individuals with disabilities. Households close to each latrine constructed will also be supported with solar lanterns to enable access at night. a total of 250 solar lanterns will be distributed. HIWA will also distribute sanitation kits to promote proper sanitation and hygiene practices. Each sanitation kit will comprise essential tools including 1 wheelbarrow, 1 pick axe, 2 shovels, 4 brooms, 3 rakes and 2 buckets.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtin the hygiene component, HIWA aims to educate and advocate for improved hygiene practices within the community. 26 Community Hygiene Promoters will undergo training to lead a comprehensive hygiene promotion campaign, disseminating crucial information through household visits, schools, feeding/nutrition centers and health facilities targeting female-headed households, persons with disabilities and individuals from marginalized communities, to protect them from waterborne diseases like AWD/choleralt/pgtltpgtltbrgtHIWA will coordinate with health, nutrition and FSL interventions through joint registration, sharing beneficiary lists and regular inter-cluster meetings which will align activities and prevent duplication and also ensure households receive complementary, integrated supportltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will be implemented in Beledweyne district in 5 villages and 8 IDP camps. The 5 villages are Dhariyow, Baslawe, Shinile, Baacad and leepow while the 8 IDP camps are Najax, Harqaboobe, Gurmad Iyo Gargar, Danyere, Budul, Alla-Suge, Nasteho and Iftin IDP camps.ltbrgtlt/pgt
